page: Amazon Web Services m7g.8xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by arm64 AWS Neoverse-V1 cores. The instance provides 32 dedicated physical cores across 32 vCPUs clocked at 2.6 GHz, operating with one thread per core to eliminate resource contention from simultaneous multithreading. Memory is provisioned at 128.0 GB, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The server includes 32 MB of L3 cache, hardware AES encryption support, a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps, zero bundled local storage, and no GPU hardware.

Benchmark data highlights strong performance in memory-intensive and parallel computing workloads. The instance achieves a top-decile PassMark memory score alongside top-quartile uncached 256 MB block read speeds of 237.87 GB/sec and write speeds of 109.3 GB/sec. Parallel CPU capability is demonstrated by a top-quartile Geekbench multi-core score of 17,159.0, complemented by high-tier database operations testing and static web serving throughput reaching 49.88 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core compute performance and stress tests fall within median percentiles, while large language model token generation exhibits low execution rates.

The 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides predictable, linear resource scaling for horizontally distributed workloads. While the absence of local NVMe storage necessitates external block storage for persistent data, the 15 Gbps network pipeline supports steady remote access. The instance offers strong resource density for mid-sized relational database engines, static web serving tiers, software compilation pipelines, and containerized microservices.
description: The Amazon Web Services m7g.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance powered by 32 dedicated arm64 AWS Neoverse-V1 cores clocked at 2.6 GHz. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor without simultaneous multithreading, each vCPU maps directly to a physical execution core. The instance provides 128.0 GB of system memory at a balanced 1:4 core-to-RAM ratio, 15 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, no integrated local storage, and zero GPUs. Benchmark profiles reveal exceptional memory performance, with PassMark memory ratings in the top tier and uncached read bandwidth exceeding 237 GB/sec, driving top-quartile results in database transactions and static web throughput. Single-thread processing and compute-heavy stress tasks place squarely within median averages, while token generation for large language models remains constrained. With predictable core scaling and high memory bandwidth efficiency, the m7g.8xlarge is well aligned for mid-to-large-scale database servers, containerized application fleets, continuous integration builds, and web serving infrastructures.
